message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1978 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick | Masterful atmosphere, iconic performances, psychological terror. |
| 1980 | **The Thing** | John Carpenter | Suspenseful paranoia, practical effects still hold up. |
| 1999 | **The Sixth Sense** | M. Night Shyamalan | Twist ending, haunting visuals, strong character arcs. |
| 2001 | **28 Days Later** | Danny Boyle | Fast‑paced zombie outbreak, gritty realism. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | James Wan | Innovative puzzle‑based horror, cult following. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Oren Peli | Found‑footage style, low budget but high tension. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | James Wan | Supernatural scares, well‑crafted mythology. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | Drew Goddard | Meta‑horror twist on tropes, clever satire. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | David Robert Mitchell | Unique premise, creepy soundtrack. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | Robert Eggers | Period authenticity, slow‑burn dread. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele | Social commentary meets horror, sharp writing. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** | John Krasinski | Silence as a weapon, emotional stakes. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster | Daylight horror, unsettling folk rituals. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Modern retelling, psychological thriller. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** | Nia DaCosta | Reimagined urban legend, strong visual style. |
| 2022 | **Evil Dead Rise** | Lee Cronin | New chapter in the franchise, visceral gore. |
| 2023 | **Nope** | Jordan Peele | Sci‑fi horror with social critique, striking imagery. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or found‑footage—and enjoy the chills!
